prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)NCCNc1nonc1/C(=N/O)Nc1ccc(F)c(Br)c1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL4685

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of IDO1 (unknown origin) assessed as reduction in kynurenine formation using L-tryptophan as substrate incubated for 60 mins by fluorescence based assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of IDO1 (unknown origin) assessed as reduction in L-kynurenine formation using L-tryptophan as substrate incubated for 30 mins by microplate spectrophotometry analysis
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call":"COMMENSURABLE","confidence":0.72,"error_class":"none","reason":"Both are high-confidence human IDO1 biochemical IC50 assays measuring inhibition of kynurenine formation with the same substrate, and the readout and incubation-time differences are unlikely to shift potency by more than 0.3 log units."}
